methods.name: Your normal month (starting level)
methods.what: The average of your last three complete months; the month in progress is left out because it is unfinished. Where EnterprateAI already shows a monthly figure on the dashboard, that figure is used, unless it is outside the usual variation of your complete months.
methods.standard: Financial modelling practice: inputs from a stated, reliable period (FAST Standard; ICAEW Financial Modelling Code)

methods.name: Growth or decline (trend)
methods.what: A straight line fitted through your last 12 complete months (least squares). It is used only if it is statistically clear: the t-statistic must be at least 2, about 95% confidence. Growth is then carried forward 'damped': each month adds 0.9 times the previous month's growth, so a run of growth is not assumed to last for ever.
methods.standard: Ordinary least squares with a t-test; damped trend (Gardner & McKenzie, 1985)

methods.name: Seasonal pattern
methods.what: Only with two years of history, and only if the differences between calendar months are larger than chance would produce (F-test, 1% level). Each calendar month then gets an index: 1.10 means 10% above an average month.
methods.standard: F-test for stable seasonality and ratio-to-moving-average indices (US Census Bureau X-11 / X-13ARIMA-SEATS)

methods.name: When you are paid
methods.what: Sales are collected after your customers' actual payment time (days sales outstanding, from your paid invoices). Money already owed is collected when due.
methods.standard: Direct-method cash flow (IAS 7); days sales outstanding

methods.name: Accounting checks
methods.what: Every month: cash = last month's cash + money in - money out; money owed to you = last month's + sales - collected; and what you own less what you owe changes by exactly the profit plus money owners put in, less what they take out. All three must hold or the run says so.
methods.standard: Integrated three-statement modelling with built-in checks (FAST Standard; ICAEW Financial Modelling Code)

methods.name: Tax, VAT, loans, payroll, equipment
methods.what: Tax on profit is set aside as profit is made (UK bands with marginal relief if chosen); VAT is collected with payments and paid over after each VAT period; loans follow their repayment schedule; employer National Insurance and pension follow your country's rules; equipment is depreciated evenly over its life.

methods.name: Low / base / high range

methods.standard: Forecast intervals from residual variation, calibrated and tested on separate data (07-phase4-changes.md)

methods.name: Verdict

methods.standard: Ordinary least squares with a t-test; damped trend (Gardner & McKenzie, 1985)

methods.name: Seasonal pattern
methods.what: Only with two years of history, and only if the differences between calendar months are larger than chance would produce (F-test, 1% level). Each calendar month then gets an index: 1.10 means 10% above an average month.
methods.standard: F-test for stable seasonality and ratio-to-moving-average indices (US Census Bureau X-11 / X-13ARIMA-SEATS)

methods.name: When you are paid
methods.what: Sales are collected after your customers' actual payment time (days sales outstanding, from your paid invoices). Money already owed is collected when due.
methods.standard: Direct-method cash flow (IAS 7); days sales outstanding

methods.name: Accounting checks
methods.what: Every month: cash = last month's cash + money in - money out; money owed to you = last month's + sales - collected; and what you own less what you owe changes by exactly the profit plus money owners put in, less what they take out. All three must hold or the run says so.
methods.standard: Integrated three-statement modelling with built-in checks (FAST Standard; ICAEW Financial Modelling Code)

methods.name: Tax, VAT, loans, payroll, equipment
methods.what: Tax on profit is set aside as profit is made (UK bands with marginal relief if chosen); VAT is collected with payments and paid over after each VAT period; loans follow their repayment schedule; employer National Insurance and pension follow your country's rules; equipment is depreciated evenly over its life.
methods.standard: HMRC and country rules for 2025/26; IAS 16 (equipment); IAS 20 (grants)

methods.name: Low / base / high range
methods.what: Revenue and costs moved by a 90% forecast range from your own history (month-to-month variation, and how sure the starting level and trend are), with payment timing and the scenario's own estimates moved too.
methods.standard: Forecast intervals from residual variation, calibrated and tested on separate data (07-phase4-changes.md)

methods.name: Verdict
methods.what: The change against doing nothing over the same months. A difference counts only if it is more than 1% of your revenue over the period. Cash is compared after loans, tax and VAT still owed.
methods.standard: Scenario analysis against a do-nothing baseline (model risk management practice, SR 11-7)

issues.what: Only 0 complete months of sales on record.
issues.why: Trend, seasonality and the usual variation cannot be measured; the projection repeats today's level.
issues.fix: Record your past invoices (at least 3 months, ideally 12 or more) or connect your accounting software.

data_quality.method: Modified z-score (Iglewicz & Hoaglin, 1993) for unusual months; record checks from your invoices and expenses.
